newsitem.title: USA: N. Ireland girl's Florida disappearance a mystery.
newsitem.headline: N. Ireland girl's Florida disappearance a mystery.

text.p: A 4-year-old girl from Northern Ireland who police believe was kidnapped from her family's hotel room had little to say about her ordeal on Tuesday, and police said they had no suspects in her abduction.
Cadihme McEvoy vanished on Sunday evening from the Orlando hotel where her family was ending a two-week vacation. She was found about 20 hours later beside a roadway about 15 miles (24 km) away.

At a news conference on Tuesday, Cadihme's parents said they believed their daughter did not fully understand what had happened to her. When asked about her disappearance, the child's only words to reporters, as she fussed and played with a Coke bottle, were: "Bye Bye Mickey Mouse!"
How the girl disappeared and resurfaced remained a mystery, police said. No suspect had been identified.

"We're basically working on the assumption that she had to have been abducted," said Jim Solomons, a spokesman for the Orange County, Florida, Sheriff. "It wouldn't have been impossible for her to walk that far on her own and not be seen by anyone, but it would have been highly improbable."

Her parents said although Cadihme is naturally friendly to strangers, she would not voluntarily get in a car with a stranger and was probably forced into a vehicle. "If there was a car involved she must have been forced in it," her father, Gerard McEvoy, said.

The girl, from Belfast, was examined at Orlando Regional Medical Centre on Monday by doctors and sex crime specialists. She was tired, cranky and hungry, and crying and clinging more than usual, the McEvoys said.
"I told her, 'I love you,' and she said, 'I love you mommy,'" Mary McEvoy said. Cadihme then heartily ate a steak dinner, although she told her parents she really wanted bacon.
She slept like a log in the same room with her parents and brother, Daclan, 8, while her sister, Janine, 9, and grandmother slept in another room.

"Anytime I would turn awake and stare at her ... My heart goes out to the mothers and fathers and brothers and sisters who haven't had the luck we've had," Gerard McEvoy said. "She has nicknames back home, but we are going to call her Cadihme Lucky."

During her medical exam, doctors noted Cadihme was tired, dehydrated and dirty but there was no visible evidence she was sexually assaulted, said Orlando Regional Medical Centre spokesman Joe Brown. Doctors were awaiting lab test results.

The family, which relocated to another Orlando hotel, had been saving for two years for their "dream vacation" -- their first trip abroad, said Gerard McEvoy. But his wife said she did not know if she would ever return to Orlando because the city now holds bad memories.
"We're lucky to be back alive," she said.

The McEvoys had intended to return to Northern Ireland on Sunday, but were staying in Orlando longer than expected pending results of the investigation. Police planned to question Cadihme again after she had rested.
Gerard McEvoy pleaded with the abductor to turn himself in. "Maybe some other poor child may not be so lucky. Obviously this person needs help."
